description.narrative:
FAO har ansökt om finansiering från Sida på 25 miljoner kronor för att genomföra projektet “Resilient rural communities for the peace building in Colombia” under perioden 2016-2019.
Insatsen är i linje med den svenska strategin för utvecklingssamarbete med Colombia 2009-2016. Strategins övergripande mål är att fattiga människor har förbättrat sina levnadsvillkor och att hållbar fred uppnås med en bred social delaktighet. Insatsen är relevant då den syftar till att utveckla resilienta lokalsamhällen och bemöta de direkta orsakerna till utsatthet, osäker livsmedelsförsörjning och undernäring, samtidigt som människors och lokala myndigheters kapacitet stärks för effektiv förberedelse inför framtida chocker. I det svenska samarbetet med Colombia ingår humanitärt stöd bl.a. i samarbete med FAO. Att bygga resiliens i Colombia är ett led i att stärka det colombianska samhället att självständigt kunna hantera den utsatta befolkningen och på sikt möjliggöra ett ökat oberoende av det humanitära stödet. Att samarbeta med FAO inom en långsiktig insats främjar en effektiv övergång från det humanitära stödet till det bilaterala. Med mångårig erfarenhet i Colombia besitter FAO en relevant kapacitet vilket ökar en ändamålsenlig användning av de svenska resurserna.
De samhällen som prioriteras i insatsen är de mest utsatta som drabbats av både konflikt och extrema väderförändringar p.g.a. ett försämrat klimat. Insatsen bidrar till jordbruksutveckling och fredsbyggande genom att: att stärka nationella myndigheters förmåga att främja resilent jordbrukspolitik i utsatta områden; att stärka lokal teknisk kapacitet för hantering (utformning, genomförande och utvärdering) av resilienta jordbrukt på landsbygden och i sårbara samhällen; och återställa möjligheten till livsmedelsförsörjning genom jordbruk i utsatta samhällen. FAO kommer att genomföra insatsen tillsammans med nationella och lokala myndigheter.

FAO has applied to Sida for funding of 25 million SEK to carry out a project called “Resilient rural communities for the peace building in Colombia” for the period 2016-2019.
The intervention aims at strengthening resilience of vulnerable rural communities affected by the conflict and extreme climatic events in prioritized areas, as a contribution to the agricultural development and peace building in Colombia by:
1) Strengthening national authorities capabilities to M&E resilient agricultural projects for rural vulnerable communities exposed to conflict and extreme weather events.
2) Strengthening local technical capacities for the management (design, implementation, and evaluation) of resilient agricultural projects in vulnerable rural communities.
3) Recovering agricultural livelihoods of vulnerable communities. FAO will implement the intervention together with national and local authorities.

Strengthen the resilience of the livelihoods of vulnerable communities affected by the conflict and extreme climatic events in prioritized areas, as a contribution to the agricultural development, environmental sustainability and peace building of Colombia.
To achieve this general objective, three specific results were defined:
R1. Strengthened technical capacities of government institutions at the national level (guidelines and guidelines) for the development, evaluation and monitoring of projects aimed at the rapid and resilient recovery of the agricultural livelihoods of vulnerable communities exposed to conflict and extreme weather events.
R2. Technical capacities of territorial actors strengthened in the management of initiatives (formulation, development and evaluation) for the rapid and resilient recovery of agricultural production systems in rural communities in vulnerable areas.
R3. Agricultural livelihoods of vulnerable communities recovered in prioritized areas, in a resilient and comprehensive manner with regards to the risks of the context.

The contribution intervention was carried out in three years. On the first year, actions were developed to strengthen national institutions; on the second year, the strengthening was for local institutions -at the departmental and municipal level- and on the third year, the focus was local, directly with communities that have been affected both by Colombia's internal armed conflict, as well as by climatic effects.
The main results achieved are:
At the national level: Strengthened the technical capacity of national institutions (guidelines and guidelines) for the awarding, evaluation and monitoring of projects aimed at the rapid and resilient recovery of the agricultural livelihoods of vulnerable communities exposed to conflict and extreme weather events. For this, a protocol was established for the identification and positioning of territories and populations with high levels of vulnerability and food and nutritional insecurity due to double effects; a guide for the incorporation of the methodology for the rapid recovery of agricultural livelihoods of vulnerable rural populations in institutional programs; a route for access to programs, resources, and services that encourage agricultural recovery and / or strengthening of food and nutritional security; and a methodological strategy for the transition to rural development of vulnerable rural communities.
At the territorial level: Strengthened technical capacity of territorial actors, in the management (formulation, implementation and evaluation) of initiatives for the rapid and resilient recovery of agricultural production systems of rural communities in vulnerable areas. For this, a training programme was designed, named "Strengthening of territorial capacities for the recovery of agricultural production, as a contribution to the construction of Peace in Colombia", which trained 197 people from 177 institutions. One of the main results of this programme was the formulation and development of 14 of the projects aimed at the recovery of the agricultural livelihoods of 2,230 rural families in the five implementing departments.
At the local level: Recovered agricultural livelihoods of vulnerable communities in prioritized areas, in a resilient and comprehensive manner that tackle context risk related to conflict and climatic events. For this 2,821 families were trained in rapid recovery of means of subsistence, 40 training demonstration centers were established, and 780 community managers were trained in the methodology of rapid recovery of livelihoods. Thanks to the contribution, the families obtained 735 tons of food and expect to produce 1,698 tons of food in the next production cycle.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
